description: A three-panel composite figure (labelled (a), (b), (c)) that mixes curve plots with a micrograph, all relating to the SPSed Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 high entropy steel. (a) is a load-controlled nanoindentation curve: Indentation Load (mN) on the y-axis (0-5000 mN) against Depth of Indentation (µm) on the x-axis (0-6 µm). The loading branch rises monotonically to a peak near 5000 mN at roughly 5.8 µm depth; the unloading branch returns to a residual depth of about 4.2 µm, leaving a large plastic impression. Blue in-panel text prints "Hardness = 7.8 ± 0.3 GPa" and "Modulus = 184 ± 5 GPa". (b) is an optical micrograph of the polished, etched surface showing a four-fold star-shaped pyramidal indent impression sitting in a granular, multi-phase speckled matrix; a white-lettered "20 µm" scale bar is drawn at the lower left. (c) is a compressive stress-strain curve, Compressive Stress (MPa) (0-2000 MPa) versus Strain (0.00-0.20), rising monotonically to approximately 2046 MPa at about 0.19 strain, with blue text printing "Compressive strength = 2046 ± 160 MPa". The group's argument is that the alloy is hard, stiff and strong in compression, with the indent in (b) being the probe whose load-displacement response is quantified in (a).

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a nanoindentation load-displacement curve with Indentation Load in mN on the y-axis (ticks at 0, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000) and Depth of Indentation in µm on the x-axis (ticks at 0, 2, 4, 6).
Panel (a) prints the values Hardness = 7.8 ± 0.3 GPa and Modulus = 184 ± 5 GPa as blue in-panel text.

In panel (a) the loading curve reaches its maximum just below the 5000 mN gridline at a depth near 6 µm, and the unloading curve ends at a residual depth between the 4 and 5 µm marks, i.e. a large plastic indentation.

Panel (b) is an optical micrograph containing a four-pointed star-shaped indentation impression (typical of a pyramidal/Vickers-type indent) in a granular multi-phase surface, with a 20 µm scale bar in the lower-left corner.

Panel (c) plots Compressive Stress (MPa) (y-axis, ticks 0, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000) against Strain (x-axis, ticks 0.00, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20) and the curve terminates at approximately 2046 MPa at a strain just below 0.20.
Panel (c) prints 'Compressive strength = 2046 ± 160 MPa' as blue in-panel text.
The caption supplied with this group is only 'Table 6 (a) (b) (c)'; it provides no descriptive text, no sample label and no scale or condition information.

The citing text describes Table 6 as listing calculated thermodynamic parameters for a non-equiatomic high entropy steel - configurational entropy (ΔSconf), mixing enthalpy (ΔHmix), size mismatch (δ), electronegativity (γ), valence electron concentration (VEC) and Ω - together with the solid-solution formation criteria; no such table or parameter values are visible in the supplied image, which instead shows two mechanical curves and one micrograph (caption vs pixels disagreement).
The citing text asserts that the VEC lies within the range for dual-phase formation and that the milled and SPSed sample forms a BCC-type structure.
The citing text asserts that the partially ordered B2-type structure in the alloy formed because of negative binary enthalpies of mixing (Al-Fe, Al-Ni being the most negative pairs).
